name: math_2_3
subject: Mathematics
substrand: Area of Part of a Circle

conflicts.fact: Sequence of when the sector area formula is taught/derived and whether it is already known
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 states students learned and write A = (θ/360°) × πr² and says 'no formula is formally taught', yet the Observe phase has them use it and the Explain phase formalises it. Lesson 2 formalises it again as established. Lesson 3 says the sector area formula comes in Lesson 4 and asks students to predict what it will look like. Lesson 4 derives it as new. Lesson 2 also says the formal derivation happens in Lesson 4, and Lesson 3 teacher says 'Yesterday we found that a slice with twice the angle has exactly twice the area'.

conflicts.fact: Sector areas for the 60° and 120° slices of radius 14 cm in Lesson 4
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 gives 102.6 cm² and 205.2 cm². With r=14, πr²=615.75, so 60° gives 102.6 and 120° gives 205.25: consistent. (No conflict in itself, but pizza radius differs across lessons: Lesson 1 and 8 use 15 cm, Lesson 4 uses 14 cm for the same pizza 'from Lesson 1'.)
Lesson 1 and Lesson 8: radius ≈ 15 cm. Lesson 4 says the same pizza diagram from Lesson 1 has radius 14 cm. Lesson 2 uses cards from radius 10 cm.

conflicts.fact: Triangle area formula/definition of the segment angle and use of sinθ
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 and 7 define the triangle area as ½r²sinθ with θ the central angle, which is correct. Lesson 7 predicts minor segment from a 'minor sector' and uses 'central angle subtended by chord'. Lesson 5 calls the 'minor sector' the area to be subtracted; Lesson 7 calls the minor/major regions 'segments' while Lesson 7 also describes a 'minor sector' with an 80° angle, mixing sector/segment terminology (Lesson 10 correctly treats minor/major sector and segment separately).

conflicts.fact: Numerical answers in Lesson 10 summative task (r=21 m, θ=80°)
conflicts.versions: Part B minor sector given as 307.9 m²; Part C major sector 1077.6 m². With r=21, πr²=1385.4, minor sector=307.9, major=1077.5: ok. Part D segment: ½r²sin80° = 217.15 in lesson, but ½·441·0.9848=217.15 so segment=90.73: ok. Lesson 7 uses the same r=21 m, θ=80° for the Eldoret farmer, treating the 80° as the minor 'sector' — no numeric conflict, but Part A arc length 29.33 m: (80/360)·2·(22/7)·21=29.33: ok.

conflicts.fact: Lesson 5's irrigation/wiper sector vs Lesson 4's pivot
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 treats a pivot arm sweeping 135° as the watered maize area at r=21 m; Lesson 5 says a centre-pivot in Laikipia has radius 80 m and waters 110°. Different examples, not conflicting.

conflicts.fact: Lesson 8 claims proportionality conjecture was first raised in Lesson 2 'when students noticed wider slices appeared more than just a bit larger'
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 raised the proportionality question as the phenomenon's central puzzle (and Lesson 1 already asserted it); Lesson 2 confirmed it with data. Lesson 3 says Lesson 2 'confirmed' it.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson started the concept map/cumulative model
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1–9 say the cumulative model started in Lesson 1. Lesson 10 teacher says 'Open your concept maps from Lesson 4'.
Lesson 1 uses π = 3.142; Lesson 9 says π ≈ 3.14159 and warns against premature rounding; Lesson 10 allows 22/7 or 3.14159.

conflicts.fact: Lesson 8 segment: sector-minus-triangle 'formula bank' vs Lesson 9 degree/radian error
conflicts.versions: Lesson 9 lists 'degrees in a radian-based formula' as an error in its overview but the actual Patient 1 error is using θ instead of θ/360; the overview lists error (1) as degrees/radians and (2) diameter, while the Lesson 9 Explain phase presents Patient 1 as omitting /360.
